Amy McFarland Caregiver LD 1717
Good Day Ladies and Gentlemen of the Veteran's and Legal Affairs Committee.
My name is Amy McFarland. I run Independence Farm with my husband.
Today I am testifying in opposition to LD# 1717. (An Act Regarding Background Checks for Medical Cannabis Providers)
This bill requires anyone applying for or renewing a registry identification card or registration certificate under the Maine Medical Use of Cannabis Act to submit to a criminal history record check.
I am not aware of any other type of farmer or farm employee in Maine that is forced to get a background check.
Now, if it is a school policy that those who enter school grounds regularly must have background checks, then I am sure many in the community would agree with that. Children need to be protected!
I suggest killing this bill, and then have the schools set a policy in place instead. Requiring a background check to all who enter school grounds regularly sounds like a better idea.
As for this issue with the 'Long-term care facility", if they have a policy about background checks for their employees and subcontractors I can understand requiring one from an individual within the cannabis industry too. Perhaps if a caregiver is going to be on their grounds for more than a week then they are required to have a background check. This should be determined between the facility and the cannabis business, the state shouldn't be interfering.
With that said, I ask you all to vote "No" on LD# 1717.

Senator Hickman, Representative Supica and Distinguished Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Veterans and Legal Affairs:
I am Matt Harrington; and I represent Senate District 33, which includes the communities of Alfred,
Lebanon, Sanford and Waterboro. I am here today to present LD 1717, "An Act Regarding
Background Checks for Medical Cannabis Providers."
No doubt you have all heard about the illegal marijuana grow houses. Well, this legislation is aimed at curtailing the people who come to Maine with false identification and set up shop, so to speak.
I submitted this legislation based on a conversation with a constituent, who is here today and will
testify in more detail as to the specific reasons this measure is needed.
The intent of this bill is not to pursue or penalize legitimately licensed medical cannabis providers
but to do all we can to stop illegal marijuana growers and sales. There is a great need to require the
same qualifications for medical providers as are required for recreational providers. Requiring complete background checks will reduce the exploitation of valid medical marijuana providers.
As I understand it, currently Maine does require a background check for medical cannabis providers; however, the check only includes Maine records. It would make sense if the check were more expansive to include all other states in order to be effective. At a minimum, this extensive check would be a bit more reassuring to those in surrounding communities in curtailing illegal grows.
Why are we giving out-of-state residents Maine licenses to operate medical cannabis facilities? As
not only a policymaker but a member of law enforcement, to protect and better serve our constituents, I believe we must employ more stringent qualifications that involve using the National Instant Criminal Background Check System (NICS) rather than just check state records.
As I mentioned, folks that will follow me will be able to provide you with additional information. I
appreciate your thoughtful attention and consideration of their testimony.
Thank you for your time.
